title: Gel DNA Extraction
author: Kenneth Schackart
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bq8smzwe

steps.title: Run gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 % w/v agarose gel in TBE (or 1.2 % w/v in TAE), load samples using a well depth of 1 mm (≈1 µL per well), and run at the recommended voltage.

steps.title: Stain gel for visualization
steps.instruction: Stain the gel according to the chosen staining method to visualize DNA bands.

steps.title: Pre‑weigh 1.5 mL tubes
steps.instruction: Label and pre‑weigh 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes for each DNA band.

steps.title: Weigh tubes with gel
steps.instruction: Place the excised gel pieces into the pre‑weighed tubes and record the total gel mass.

steps.title: Excise DNA band
steps.instruction: Place the gel on a transilluminator, use a clean blunted scalpel to cut out the desired band; each extraction column can process up to 1 g agarose.

steps.title: Add binding buffer
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL Binding Buffer per 100 mg gel (1:1 v:w). For gels >2 % w/v agarose, use a 2:1 volume‑to‑weight ratio.

steps.title: Dissolve gel at 55 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 55 °C, inverting occasionally, until the gel is completely dissolved.

steps.title: Adjust solution color
steps.instruction: If the solution is orange or violet, add 10 µL of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and mix well; a yellow color is desired.

steps.title: Add precipitation reagent
steps.instruction: If fragment ≤500 bp, add isopropanol equal to the gel volume (e.g., 100 µL to 100 mg gel in 100 µL buffer). If fragment >10 kb, add water equal to the gel volume. Mix well.

steps.title: Load gel solution onto column
steps.instruction: Transfer gel solution to the extraction column and centrifuge, using a counter‑balance.

substeps.instruction: Transfer up to 800 µL of gel solution to the column; if the volume exceeds 800 µL, load in stages.
Prepare a counter‑balance by matching tube weight (weigh tube, add water to a second tube until weights match; add 1 µL water per 1 mg difference).
Discard the flow‑through and place the column back in the same collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash steps with a fresh counter‑balance.

substeps.instruction: Add 700 µL wash buffer to the column.
Prepare a new counter‑balance (weights may have changed).
Discard the flow‑through and keep the column in the collection tube.

steps.title: Spin empty column
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the empty column to remove residual wash buffer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g, °C, for an additional 1 min.

steps.title: Elute DNA from column
steps.instruction: Elute purified DNA into a clean tube.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the column to a clean 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 50 µL elution buffer to the center of the membrane (20‑50 µL acceptable, not less than 10 µL).
